To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
media education in the countries of the Commonwealth of Independent States is developing, but the development of media education is not the same in all countries.
the development of media education in CIS countries has a lot of similarities, but at the same time there is a certain diversity in the development of media culture and media education programs.
media education in the countries of the CIS is a complex process, and it is impossible to create a unified model for its implementation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of mass communication and media education in the countries of the Commonwealth of independent States (CIS) as a new and important area of research and practice in the field of mass communication and journalism.

the following issues: what are the most effective methods of media education, how should the media education program look like, how can the mass media education system be improved, how to develop media education in the countries of the Commonwealth of independent States.
a comparative analysis of the development and content of media education programs in the CIS countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
media education is a necessary component of the educational system of any country and its development in the CIS countries should be carried out on a common basis.

the development of media education in CIS countries is an urgent task that requires the attention and support of the state, society, and media professionals, and it should be based on the principles of democracy, freedom of expression, and the development of a critical mind.

media education is a complex of educational activities aimed at the formation of a positive attitude of the audience (including children and adolescents) to the media and media culture, the ability to use the information and communication resources of the media, the formation of a responsible attitude of the audience to the media as a factor of social development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the media education of the citizens of the CIS countries should be based on the principles of the democratic state, the rule of law, the supremacy of the Constitution, the equality of all citizens regardless of their ethnic and national origin, the principles of freedom of speech and the media, the principles of the freedom of conscience, the principles of respect for the rights and freedoms of man and citizen, and the principles of the inviolability of human dignity and human rights and freedoms.
the development of media education in all CIS countries should be based on the principles of democracy, freedom of speech and freedom of information.
media education should be based on sociocultural rather than on ideological concepts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

media education in the modern world is a complex and multi-level process, the development of which is impossible without the use of modern technologies, and the most important of them are the Internet technologies.

the media education of the population in the CIS countries should be based on the principles of tolerance, respect for the rights and freedoms of other people, and the desire to understand the diversity and complexity of the modern world.
the development of mass communication education in the CIS should not be based on confrontation and propaganda.
